newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY WELCOMES EU ENLARGEMENT RECOMMENDATION.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY WELCOMES EU ENLARGEMENT RECOMMENDATION.

text.p: Hungary welcomed on Tuesday the formal decision by the European Commission to recommend Poland, the Czech Republic, Hungary, Slovenia, Estonia and Cyprus for a first wave of EU entry talks.
"Hungary was pleased to see another firm commitment from the Commission to enlarging the European Union," Hungarian foreign ministry spokesman Gabor Horvath told Reuters.
"We are convinced that the indication that Hungary will be included in the first round of enlargement is a clear recognition that Hungary has satisfied the criteria of accession."

The Commission adopted the recommendation document, Agenda 2000, without much discussion during a meeting of EU Commissioners in Strasbourg, France, ahead of their formal presentation of the decision to the European Parliament on Wednesday.

The decision means that Latvia, Lithuania, Slovakia, Bulgaria and Romania will have to wait for membership although they will each have contractual accession partnerships allowing them to prepare at their own speed for joining.
The Commission's proposal will not be the last word on who will negotiate EU entry as it could be overturned by EU governments, which have different national interests at stake.
A final decision will be taken by EU leaders at their Luxembourg summit in December.
Horvath said he foresaw no problem in the European Union accepting the Commision's recommendation in the case of Hungary.

"We expect there to be a lively discussion but in the case of Hungary national parliaments as well as other institutional decision-making bodies of the European Union will not find any areas which will disqualify Hungary from being included," he said.

He added that feedback Hungary had received so far from the European Commission to the questionnaire it had completed to enable the Comminssion to make its recommendation had been "realistic, balanced as well as overwhelmingly positive".
"However, we definitely expect that (Agenda 2000) will point out a few areas in which we will have to work," he said.

Horvath welcomed the inclusion in the Commission's list of Estonia, a former Soviet Republic which along with the other Baltic states of Lithuania and Latvia failed to make the first round of NATO enlargement announced last week.
"This is the first enlargement round where they are taking in a country from the former Soviet bloc," he said.
"By this the EU is giving a clear indication for openness, for enlargement as well as underlining for the chance for all countries who meet the criteria to qualify for starting accession talks."
